headlines: Intuitive Machines Q3 Earnings Today: Wall Street and options markets' last-minute verdict on LUNR stock (TipRanks, 2026-11-12)
What Does Intuitive Machines (LUNR) Winning CLPS 2 Mean For It (Simply Wall St, 2026-11-10)
Intuitive Machines Announces Date for Third Quarter 2026 Results - Nov 12 before market open, 8:30 am ET (FT Markets, 2026-10-29)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Intuitive Machines reports Q3 2026 before the open today (Nov 12, 8:30 am ET), so this gap is positioning INTO the print - no results had been released as of this 08:08 ET scan. The structural setup behind the bid: NASA selected LUNR for CLPS 2, a lunar-delivery program valued at up to $10B, and backlog had already climbed to $1.8B as of Jun 30 2026 from $213.1M at Dec 31 2025, on Q2 revenue of $206M. TipRanks notes the options market is pricing a ~13.7% post-earnings move against a ~$29 average analyst target.
gappers.why: Pre-earnings positioning layered on a genuine contract catalyst. The CLPS 2 award turns an up-to-$10B program into a credible backlog pipeline, and momentum buyers are front-running a possible second straight record-revenue, positive-adjusted-EBITDA quarter.
gappers.impact: Least sustainable of the five at this exact moment, because the event has not happened yet. Options-implied ~13.7% means roughly this entire gap can be erased or doubled in one print at 8:30 ET. LUNR has already shown violent two-way swings this month (+16% -> -16% -> -8% -> +22% per Schwab Network). Pre-market volume of 1.21M is the thinnest of the five, so the gap is real but lightly traded. No sector read-through: space infrastructure is uncorrelated to today's AI-complex selloff, which is a point in its favor on a day when most of this list is bleeding.
gappers.horizon_reason: A pre-print gap is by definition headline-driven and binary; the CLPS 2 thesis could become LONG_TERM, but only once the 8:30 ET numbers and guidance are in hand.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing - the book is 100% cash, 0 positions, 0/3 weekly trades used. The real cost is the 2:1 R:R test: entering a +12.6% pre-print gap puts any honest stop below a gap that may not hold, while the strategy bans stops within 3% of price. It also fails the Entry Checklist, which needs a documented catalyst already in the price, and the Confluence rule's >=2-of-{VWAP,RSI,200-SMA,insider} agreement cannot be assessed on an unprinted quarter. Buying a binary 20 minutes before it resolves is the opposite of 'patience > activity' - let the print land and re-evaluate on the 09:00/10:00 ET run.

headlines: NBIS Retreats After CoreWeave Rally Ahead Of Q3 Report; analyst says market can't squeeze out top players amid record cloud demand (Stocktwits, 2026-11-12)
Nebius Group Q3 2026 Earnings Date and Estimates - scheduled Nov 12 2026 (MarketBeat, 2026-11-12)
NVDA falls amid further CEO allegations; board meeting to consider removal (Newsquawk, 2026-11-12)
AI jitters erupt after Democrats threaten data centre build-out - 20 most valuable AI and chip stocks lost more than $1 trillion in one week (Dealroom, 2026-11-12)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nebius reports Q3 2026 today (Nov 12). Consensus per Koyfin is revenue +521% YoY to ~$907.2M with an adjusted loss of ~$0.63/share, versus -$0.40 a year ago. The drop is not company-specific news - it is the AI complex repricing. Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang and NVDA fell sharply (reported between 4% and 7.8% across outlets, and -7.48% on this run's own tape read), while Washington-side threats to data-centre build-out have knocked more than $1 trillion off the 20 most valuable AI and chip names in a week. NBIS had been +11.7% pre-bell on Nov 11 on CoreWeave's strong print and has now given all of it back and more.
gappers.why: Multiple compression on a pre-profit, capex-heavy neocloud. NBIS trades on a ~$7-9B end-2026 ARR target, so when the market questions whether AI capex keeps compounding - via political risk to data-centre permitting and governance risk at the sector's anchor vendor - terminal value is what gets marked down first, and hardest in the highest-multiple, cash-burning names.
gappers.impact: Pre-market volume of 7.31M is the heaviest of the five by a wide margin, and the move is sector-wide rather than idiosyncratic, which argues against a clean one-day mean-revert. Read-through is explicit and two-way: CRWV is down almost identically (-10.15%) on the same tape, so this is a factor move, not a stock move. It also will not resolve on technicals - today's Q3 print is the binary that decides direction. Note this run's own deterioration signal: NBIS was only -1.33% on the 07:12 ET tape read and is -10.22% an hour later.
gappers.horizon_reason: The proximate driver is a headline-driven sector derating plus an unresolved earnings event, not a structural change at Nebius; the $7-9B ARR thesis is intact but unconfirmed until today's print.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces no existing holding (0 open positions, 0/3 weekly trades). Within today's own list NBIS and CRWV are the same bet - owning both would trip the correlation gate (>0.75 against 2+ open positions), so at most one neocloud is ownable, and CRWV is the better-documented of the two because its results are actually in hand. On R:R: catching a -10% knife into its own earnings print cannot clear 2:1 at a sane stop, since any stop wide enough to survive a post-earnings gap leaves ATR-based 1.0%-of-equity sizing with a position too small to matter. The 'exit a sector after 2 failed trades' rule and the long-bias filter both argue for watching, not catching.

headlines: CoreWeave Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results - FY26 capex guidance raised at the low end to $37-39B (CoreWeave IR, 2026-11-10)
CoreWeave Q3: revenue jumped 168%, $132.5B revenue backlog, up from $104B (CNBC, 2026-11-10)
CoreWeave Q3 Revenue Surges 168% but Capex Soars - net loss $709M, capex $14.511B (TradingKey, 2026-11-10)
AI jitters erupt after Democrats threaten data centre build-out (Dealroom, 2026-11-12)
gappers.catalyst_detail: CoreWeave reported strong Q3 on Nov 10: revenue +168% YoY, revenue backlog $132.5B (up from $104B), but a $709M net loss and $14.511B of quarterly capex, with full-year 2026 capex guidance raised at the low end to $37-39B from $35-39B. The stock spiked on the print (reported +15% to +27% across outlets) and closed Nov 11 at $60.77. Today's -10.15% is give-back driven by the same two sector shocks hitting NBIS - the Nvidia CEO investigation and political threats to data-centre build-out - with no fresh CoreWeave-specific news found.
gappers.why: The backlog-versus-capex trade flipping sign. On Nov 10 the market paid for the $132.5B backlog; two days later it is discounting the $37-39B of capex and the rising debt needed to serve that backlog. Once data-centre build-out itself becomes a political risk, a company whose entire equity story is 'spend $38B to convert backlog' is the most levered expression of that risk.
gappers.impact: Volume is the tell: 4.93M shares pre-market on top of an enormous 165.2M prior full session is consistent with genuine two-way repricing rather than a thin headline spike. But the direction of travel is a round-trip of a two-day-old earnings pop, which is textbook post-event fade rather than fresh distribution. Sector read-through is direct and already visible in NBIS (-10.22%) - treat these as one position, not two. This also deepened within today: CRWV was -7.24% on the 07:12 ET scan and is -10.15% now.
gappers.horizon_reason: The Q3 backlog is structural, but the proximate move is a sentiment and factor unwind of a two-day-old spike; nothing in the business changed between Nov 10 and today.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing on a flat book. Against NBIS it is the better of the two neocloud expressions - actual reported results rather than an unprinted quarter - so if the strategy ever takes one, CRWV is the one that can be underwritten. It still fails R:R here: a second-day fade with no support level established puts the nearest honest stop below the pre-earnings base in the mid-$40s, roughly 15-20% away, which would demand a $65+ target to clear 2:1 and blows through ATR-based 1.0%-risk sizing. The cheap version of this trade is waiting for a base to form; the expensive version is catching the fade today.

headlines: PepGen (NASDAQ:PEPG) Surges on Positive FREEDOM2 DM1 Data Despite In-Line Q3 Results (ChartMill, 2026-11-10)
PepGen spotlights 46.5% mean splicing correction in Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 10 mg/kg cohort (Market Chameleon, 2026-11-10)
PepGen (NASDAQ:PEPG) Stock Price Target Raised at Wedbush; shares rose 92.9% (MarketBeat, 2026-11-11)
PepGen Q3 Results Show Modest Loss Miss and Extended Cash Runway With New Trial Data (Tickeron, 2026-11-12)
gappers.catalyst_detail: On Nov 10 PepGen reported positive Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 results for PGN-EDODM1 in myotonic dystrophy type 1 at the 10 mg/kg cohort: a 46.5% mean splicing correction at Week 13, described as the highest reported, with improvements across multiple functional measures. The stock re-rated violently, quoted between +92.9% and +148% intraday on over 70M shares. Q3 itself was unremarkable - a $19.4M net loss, $0.28/share, a penny worse than the $0.27 consensus - though the company also flagged an extended cash runway. Wedbush raised its price target on Nov 11. Today's +5.51% is third-day continuation drift, not the initial catalyst.
gappers.why: A binary de-risking event in a clinical-stage biotech. The 46.5% splicing-correction figure re-rates the probability that PGN-EDODM1 works at all, which in a pre-revenue name moves the whole NPV rather than an earnings line. The same trial carried an FDA partial clinical hold in March 2026 that knocked the stock over 20%, so this readout also clears a standing overhang - which is why the re-rate was violent rather than incremental.
gappers.impact: The initial move looks real rather than a headline spike: over 70M shares on a ~$5 stock is genuine institutional repositioning, and a sell-side target raise followed. But today's +5.5% is the low-conviction part of the sequence - the easy money was Nov 10, and third-day drift on a doubled biotech is where momentum chasers get caught. Pre-market volume of 762k is the second-thinnest here. The dominant forward risk is dilution: this is a cash-burning clinical name whose runway has been the standing concern, and a doubled share price is exactly when such a company raises equity. No sector read-through, and usefully uncorrelated to today's AI unwind.
gappers.horizon_reason: The catalyst is structural - a dose-cohort readout that changes the asset's probability of success and clears a prior FDA hold - and healthcare is the favored sector in the mid-cycle row of TRADING-STRATEGY.md's rotation table, the phase this book has been positioning for; worth a multi-day/week swing on a pullback, not on day three of a vertical move.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing on a flat book, and it is the most interesting name here precisely because it is NOT part of the AI-complex trade that makes NBIS and CRWV one correlated bet - it passes the correlation gate trivially. Honest R:R read: it can clear 2:1, but not at this price. After a near-double, ATR(14) is hugely inflated, so ATR-based sizing at 1.0% equity risk yields a small position, and any stop outside the 3% minimum distance sits deep inside the gap. The genuine competing use of capital is the already-queued XLV/XLP entry, which is lower beta and expresses the same mid-cycle healthcare read - PEPG is the high-variance version of a thesis the book already has a boring way to own.

headlines: Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) Announces ETH Holdings Reach 6.05 Million Tokens, and Total Crypto and Total Cash & Marketable Securities (FT Markets, 2026-10-26)
BitMine Immersion Crypto Treasuries - treasury valued at $12.63B, 100% allocated to Ethereum (6,070,092 ETH) (CoinGecko)
Bitmine Immersion (BMNR) Announces ETH Holdings Reach 5.81 Million Tokens, Total Crypto and Cash of $11.6B (RBC Richardson Barr, 2026-10-23)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No BitMine-specific catalyst surfaced for today - both the dated ticker-news query and a crypto-selloff query returned zero results, and BMNR's own most recent disclosures are treasury updates rather than events: ETH holdings rising to roughly 6.05-6.07M tokens, about 2% of supply, with crypto plus cash and marketable securities around $11.6-12.6B as of late October. BMNR is also the only one of the five with a genuinely fresh, tight two-sided quote at scan time (bid $17.90 / ask $17.99 at 08:11 ET), so the -5.15% is a real liquid print rather than a thin mark.
gappers.why: Pure beta to Ethereum. BMNR is effectively a levered ETH holding company - essentially 100% of a ~$12.6B treasury allocated to Ethereum against an ~$18 share price - so the equity tracks ETH spot plus a sentiment premium or discount to NAV. With no company news, a -5% move is the market marking the treasury down, likely compounded by the same broad risk-off hitting high-beta AI and crypto-adjacent names together.
gappers.impact: Thin on evidence, which is itself the finding: a 5% move with no locatable catalyst is a NAV and beta move, not an information event, so it carries no edge in either direction. It has the tightest quote of the five and healthy liquidity, so the price is trustworthy even though the story is absent. Read-through is to crypto-treasury proxies generally rather than to anything in the current book. Note it was -5.04% at 07:12 ET and dropped below the 5% threshold on that run's 07:24 ET verification pass, so it is a borderline rather than a decisive gapper.
gappers.horizon_reason: No durable thesis and no catalyst; the move is a derivative of an asset price rather than a change in the business.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing, and it is the clearest decline of the five. It has the weakest claim on capital here: the smallest gap at -5.15%, barely over the threshold and already borderline, zero documented catalyst, and a thesis that reduces to 'long ETH' - which is not a stock thesis and which the strategy has no mandate for. Taking it would burn one of three weekly trades on unlevered crypto beta while a documented biotech re-rate (PEPG) and the queued healthcare rotation entry (XLV/XLP) both rank ahead of it. It cannot be assessed against the 2:1 R:R minimum at all, because there is no catalyst-defined target to measure reward against.
